fields.v: Benchmark input (not an approach): one real user requirement per task (text, optionally images or URLs), merged to single turn; ground-truth checklists per requirement for functionality, visual design and content (LLM-inferred, human-merged and validated). Output: a single native HTML web app

No prescribed flow: each LLM generates one artifact per requirement from identical system prompts (agents: requirement and control prompt entered manually); artifacts then scored automatically on 24 metrics; z-scores weighted by survey-derived weights into an overall score. Benchmark construction: 5,000 sampled online requirements -> multi-turn merge (experts + Gemini-2.5-pro) -> three-expert filtering and MinHash/MiniLM deduplication -> checklist generation by 3 LLMs and human merge

fields.v: Tasks: 1,572 real user requirements (agents: random 165). Configurations: 12 LLMs via standard APIs with recommended parameters and identical system prompts; 2 agents via web interfaces with appended control prompts restricting output to native HTML. Baseline: none (z-scores relative to the mean over all models). Held constant: requirements, system prompt, single artifact per requirement, metrics; images described by Gemini-2.5-pro for uni-modal LLMs. Acceptance tests: none; checklists judged by LLM plus rule-based tools. Repetitions: single generation per requirement. Human intervention: manual entry for agents

GPT-5-High best overall (13.81%), GLM-4.5 second (11.76%, only model above average on all nine perspectives), MiniMax-M2 third (7.89%); GPT-4o worst (-38.65%, below average on all perspectives). No model dominates all 24 metrics. Open-source gap to GPT-5-High under 6%. Agents above average but below expectations (MiniMax Agent below its base MiniMax-M2), strong on alignment, weaker on performance and visual quality. Generalist models beat coder variants (Qwen3-Instruct > Qwen3-Coder-Plus; GPT-5-High > GPT-5-Codex). Vague and highly complex requirements scored higher; image inputs lowered scores (-8.68%). No significance tests between models

Distinguished models and gave per-perspective profiles; authors argue small weighted z-score differences (most within 3%) can be meaningful but give no test. Judge stability checked (run variance significantly lower than between-model variance). Agents scored on a different subset than LLMs. Limitations stated: front-end/native HTML only; dataset and metric implementation not released; dataset distribution, annotation reliability, metric design and metric correctness/stability may affect results

Six limitations: only front-end native HTML (backend and frameworks future work); dataset and metric implementations cannot be released for legal reasons (another open batch planned); dataset distribution may influence results; manual annotation reliability; metric design choices; metric correctness and stability. Gaps: no model dominates all metrics; targeted model optimisation needed

Agents evaluated on 165 requirements vs LLMs on 1,572, yet ranked together in Table 4 (z-scores over different samples). Abstract says 'no dominant model across all evaluation metrics' while GPT-5-High leads overall; the 'less than a 6% gap' compares weighted z-score sums (GLM-4.5 11.76% vs GPT-5-High 13.81%). Perspective weights in Figure 4 differ from the 'ALL' column of Table 6 (e.g. Functional Alignment 14.07% vs 13.8%, Content Alignment 12.75% vs 12.5%, Visual Alignment 9.46% vs 9.7%, Visual Quality 8.92% vs 9.0%). Values from Table 4. Data: results on Hugging Face (huggingface.co/spaces/CompileError/WebCoderBench); dataset and metric implementation not released. Prompts given in Appendix F. No pre-registration. Programming language: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (generated); evaluation tooling language not stated
